newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Ethiopia urged to free 84 detained businessmen.
newsitem.headline: Ethiopia urged to free 84 detained businessmen.

text.p: An Ethiopian rights group has appealed to the government to release 84 businessmen detained on charges of leading a protest against sharp rent increases.
The Ethiopian Human Rights Council said the businessmen shut their shops on May 19 to draw attention of the authorities to a rise of up to 40,000 percent in rent for state-owned houses.
"To protest in a legal and peaceful manner for citizens to express their grievances is a constitutional right," the human rights group said in a statement issued on Tuesday.
Some 1,300 business premises were sealed off by authorities and 84 people who were suspected to have coordinated the strike were detained, according to business and council sources.
Of the total, 29 also lost their licences and the cases of 200 others were still pending. The balance appealed for pardon and had their shops reopened, according to the city council.
The group said that the revoking of trade licences without court orders violated human and constitutional rights.
The group said it considered as unfair a decision by the Addis Ababa City Council to force businessmen to admit errors and appeal for pardon for their shops to reopen.

The council has said that the rent increase was minimal compared to rents charged by private house owners. It also says that it required the rent income for the maintenance of city utilities such as roads.
